lesson_title: Mechanical Energy: The Wallet Physics Seals
hook_text: Every falling object carries a sealed wallet with two pockets — and physics counts every cent.
clip_script: Picture a wallet with exactly two pockets, carried by every object that moves near the Earth. Pocket one is the HEIGHT pocket: money lands in it whenever the object climbs. Pocket two is the SPEED pocket: money lands in it whenever the object speeds up. Physics calls the money energy — and here is the rule the whole lesson stands on: while nothing rubs — no friction, no air resistance — the wallet is SEALED. Coins may stream between the two pockets as fast as they like, but not one cent can enter or leave the wallet itself. Drop something, and money pours from the height pocket into the speed pocket the whole way down. The total never moves.
visual_style: Animated wallet strapped to a falling ball, coins streaming between glowing height and speed pockets as the ball drops past floor markers; totals ticker holding steady at 588.
mood: Satisfying bookkeeping — chaos of a fall revealed as perfect accounting.
pacing: Calm setup of the two pockets, accelerating coin-stream as the ball falls, freeze-frame audit at three heights, clean landing beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any fall's speed straight out of the wallet — no stopwatch needed.
